findings.finding: The specs use two status levels, vocabulary status and version status, but no criterion says how they relate. A builder cannot tell what deprecating or reactivating a vocabulary does to its versions, which status the list shows, or whether a deprecated vocabulary can get a new version.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18175/AC1: 'the API updates the vocabulary status to the requested value (`ACTIVE` or `DEPRECATED`)'; SIMPL-18170/AC2: 'the vocabulary status is `ACTIVE` by default and can later be manually changed to `DEPRECATED` or back to `ACTIVE`'; SIMPL-18186/AC1: 'the system automatically sets its status to ACTIVE' (vocabulary or version); BP02B.05: 'Full Vocabulary Deprecation - all versions deprecated when obsolete'; OpenAPI PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName} returns VocabularyCategory with 'version: 3 ... status: DEPRECATED'; SIMPL-18559/AC2: 'there is no ACTIVE version available for this vocabulary'.
findings.question: When the vocabulary status is set to DEPRECATED or back to ACTIVE, what happens to the status of each version, which status does GET /vocabularies show, and can a new version be created for a DEPRECATED vocabulary (and if so, does the vocabulary become ACTIVE)?
options: Vocabulary status is a separate flag; version statuses do not change
Deprecating the vocabulary deprecates all versions; reactivating restores only the latest version to ACTIVE
Vocabulary status is derived from the latest version status (one status, not two)

findings.finding: The role model is named five different ways and the criteria do not say which role may read and which may write. With a read-only role and an admin role in the notes, the blanket 403 rule can be read two ways.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18196/AC2: 'I do not have the vocabulary management role ... When I invoke any Vocabulary Management API endpoint Then the API returns a `403 Forbidden` response'; SIMPL-18196 notes: '`GA_VOCABULARY_VIEWER`: for read-only operations', '`GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN`: for both read and write operations'; SIMPL-18196/AC4: 'the Tier1 Role validation'; SIMPL-18176/AC1: 'a role authorizing read access to the vocabulary history'; SIMPL-18559/AC1: 'with any role'; SIMPL-18184/AC1: 'vocabulary management admin rights'; OpenAPI OAuth2Auth scopes 'read', 'write'.
findings.question: Which roles exist for this component, which operations and screens does each role allow, and is 'the vocabulary management role' in the criteria GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN only, or either of the two roles? Is the check done by the gateway (Tier 1) or by the service?
options: GA_VOCABULARY_VIEWER may call all GET endpoints and see all read screens; only GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN may create, version or change status; anyone else gets 403
Only GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN may use the API and UI at all (viewer role not built)
Any authenticated Governance Authority user may read (SIMPL-18559 'any role'); write needs GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN

findings.finding: The criterion blocks a new version that references a deprecated vocabulary version, while the OpenAPI creates the version and returns a warning for exactly that case, and the process says deprecated vocabularies can still be referenced.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18184/AC2: 'the validation fails for each referenced version with status _DEPRECATED_ And the new vocabulary version is not created'; OpenAPI POST /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions 201 example: 'validationWarnings: code: deprecatedVocabularyReference, description: Referenced internal vocabulary 'LegacyVocabulary' version 1 is deprecated.'; BP 2B.6: 'A deprecated vocabulary can still be used and referenced, but this will be discouraged.'; SIMPL-18184/AC4 shows only a warning.
findings.question: Does a reference to a DEPRECATED internal vocabulary version block creation (400) or create the version with a warning (201 with validationWarnings)?
options: Block: 400 with one issue per deprecated reference, nothing created (story)
Warn: 201 with a deprecatedVocabularyReference warning per reference (OpenAPI and BP)

findings.finding: The negative scenario returns 'errors or warnings' and then does not create the vocabulary, so it reads as if warnings also block. The story note and the OpenAPI treat warnings as non-blocking.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18183/AC2: 'a structured list of semantic errors or warnings is returned And the vocabulary or vocabulary version is not created'; SIMPL-18183 note: 'we issue warnings for external vocabularies that cannot be resolved'; OpenAPI VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse.validationWarnings: 'Non-blocking validation warnings returned when vocabulary creation succeeds despite warnings.'
findings.question: Do semantic warnings (for example an unresolved external namespace) stop creation, or is creation refused only when there is at least one semantic error?
options: Only errors block; warnings are returned in the 201 response
Errors and warnings both block creation

findings.finding: No spec lists the syntax, structure and semantic rules, so a tester cannot build a passing and a failing vocabulary for each criterion. The UI story also names a 'structure' check that the API stories do not have.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18180/AC6: 'the uploaded or submitted vocabulary file violates required structure rules'; SIMPL-18183/AC1: 'the vocabulary has correct semantics'; SIMPL-18182 So that: 'terms are unique, consistent, and logically coherent'; SIMPL-18182/AC2: 'a vocabulary version is semantically valid'; SIMPL-18181 covers 'syntax validation only'; BP02B.01: 'according to defined syntactic and structural rules'; OpenAPI semanticError example: 'Literal value for object property'.
findings.question: Which rules make up structure validation and semantic validation (with one example per rule), and is 'structure' a separate step from 'semantic' or the same thing under another name?
options: Structure validation is part of semantic validation (two steps: syntax, semantic)
Structure validation is a third step between syntax and semantic, with its own rule list

findings.finding: Validation must run when a file is uploaded, before submission, but the API offers no validate-only operation and the API story states there is no separate validation endpoint.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18180/AC1: 'When I upload a vocabulary file in the UI Then the system automatically performs syntax and structure validation on the uploaded file'; SIMPL-18180/AC2: 'When I submit a new vocabulary via the UI Then the system performs syntax and structure validation as part of the submission flow'; SIMPL-18183 So that: 'without a separate validation endpoint'; OpenAPI: validation only on POST /vocabularies and POST /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions.
findings.question: Where does validation on upload run: in the browser, through a new validate-only endpoint, or not at all (validation only on submit)?
options: UI parses the Turtle file in the browser on upload (syntax only); full validation on submit
Add a validate-only endpoint to the API
No validation on upload; AC1 is met by validation on submit

findings.finding: The creation form must not show a change log field, but the API requires a changelog to create a vocabulary.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18169/AC1: 'the following required fields are available: Name, Description, File upload And no field for version or change log is displayed'; OpenAPI CreateVocabularyPayload required: 'vocabularyFile, name, description, changelog'.
findings.question: What changelog value does the UI send when creating a vocabulary, or should changelog be optional on POST /vocabularies?
options: UI sends a fixed text such as 'Initial version.'
Make changelog optional for POST /vocabularies
Show a change log field on the creation form

findings.finding: It is unclear whether a new version can be created from a metadata change alone. 'and/or' allows it, 'including ... uploading an updated file' and the API (file required) do not, and AC1 promises a form pre-filled with the content.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18172/AC2: 'When I update the metadata and/or vocabulary content, including providing a change summary and uploading an updated file'; SIMPL-18172/AC1: 'a form pre-filled with the existing vocabulary metadata and content'; OpenAPI CreateNewVocabularyVersionPayload required: 'vocabularyFile, description, changelog'.
findings.question: Must the user upload a new file for every new version, or may the UI resend the current content when only the description changes? What does 'pre-filled with ... content' show?
options: File upload is mandatory for each new version; the form shows the current file name only
Metadata-only change is allowed; the UI resubmits the current content as the file

findings.finding: The UI example filters on a part of the name in lower case, while the API name filter accepts only a full PascalCase name.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18163/AC1: 'When I apply a filter (e.g., "Vocabulary Status = Deprecated" or "Name contains 'shacl'")'; OpenAPI VocabularyNameQuery: 'Filter by vocabulary name. Must be in PascalCase, alphanumeric', pattern '^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$'.
findings.question: Is the name filter a case-insensitive 'contains' search or an exact name match?
options: Contains, case-insensitive: the API name filter must change
Exact PascalCase match: the UI example is wrong
UI filters the loaded page on the client side

findings.finding: The story is about a Schema Manager endpoint for Metadata Quality Profiles that is not in the Vocabulary Management API, and its note puts the only Vocabulary Manager part out of scope. A builder of this component cannot tell whether to build it.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-28680/AC1: 'I submit a `POST` request to `/metadataQualityProfiles/{metadataQualityProfileName}/versions`'; SIMPL-28680/AC2: 'When Schema Manager processes the update'; link: 'simpl-schema-manager/.../t1-schema-openapi.yaml'; note: 'the Metadata Quality Profile vocabulary needs to be present there (out of scope)'.
findings.question: Is SIMPL-28680 part of the Vocabulary Manager build, or only of Schema Manager? If the MQP vocabulary must exist in Vocabulary Manager, is that seed data for this component?
options: Out of scope for Vocabulary Manager; drop from this component
In scope only as seed data: the MQP vocabulary is loaded into Vocabulary Manager
In scope: build the MQP endpoints here

findings.finding: Several criteria require 403 and an authentication error, but no operation in the OpenAPI declares 401 or 403.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18196/AC2: 'returns a `403 Forbidden` response'; SIMPL-18196/AC3: 'returns an authentication error response'; SIMPL-18162/AC3: 'error message 403 Forbidden'; SIMPL-18173/AC4: 'rejected due to insufficient permissions'; SIMPL-18173/AC5: 'not authenticated ... the request is rejected'; OpenAPI responses per operation: 200/201/204, 400, 404, 406, 409, 413, 415, 500 only; security 'OAuth2 authentication provided by the gateway'.
findings.question: Are 401 and 403 returned by the gateway or by the service, with which body (problem+json?), and should the OpenAPI list them?
options: Gateway returns 401/403; service never sees unauthenticated calls
Service returns 401/403 as problem+json and the OpenAPI is extended

findings.finding: The process has a manual review in validation and a publish step by the Governance Authority, while the stories publish automatically right after automated validation.
findings.evidence: BP02B.02: 'semantic validation is performed through a combination of automated checks and manual review'; BP 2B.5: 'The Governance Authority publishes a new vocabulary'; SIMPL-18186 So that: 'I do not require a manual publication action'; SIMPL-18187: 'automatically persisted and made available'.
findings.question: Is the manual review a step outside the system (before upload), or does the component need a review or approval state before publication?
options: Manual review happens before upload; no state in the system
Add a review state before a version becomes ACTIVE

findings.finding: The accepted file formats and the upload size limit are not stated in any criterion. The process names RDF Schema and OWL, the API accepts Turtle only and has a 5 MB limit.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18169/AC2: 'The uploaded file format is supported'; BP02B.01: 'creates a new vocabulary using RDF Schema or OWL'; SIMPL-395: 'files are ttl'; OpenAPI vocabularyFile: 'Vocabulary file in Turtle format'; OpenAPI 413 example: 'The maximum allowed upload size is 5 MB'.
findings.question: Which file formats (Turtle only, or also RDF/XML, OWL/XML, JSON-LD) and which maximum size apply, and what does the UI show when the file is too large?
options: Turtle only, 5 MB, as in the OpenAPI
Several RDF serialisations, converted to Turtle on upload

findings.finding: The version identifier format is left to 'the versioning algorithm' and 'the same versioning library as schema management', while the API uses an integer and SIMPL-18170 starts at 1.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18189/AC1: 'the next version identifier based on the versioning algorithm'; SIMPL-18190/AC1: 'the subsequent version number based on the applicable versioning algorithm'; SIMPL-18173 and SIMPL-18190 technical info: 'incremental using the same versioning library as schema management'; OpenAPI version: 'type: integer, minimum: 1'; SIMPL-18170/AC1: 'version `1`'.
findings.question: Is the next version always the previous integer plus 1?
options: Integer, previous plus 1
Another scheme from the schema management library (for example semantic versions)

findings.finding: The API lets a single version status be changed by hand, but no story covers it, and the stories assume only the newest version is ACTIVE. A builder must guess whether two versions may be ACTIVE and which ones a new version deprecates.
findings.evidence: OpenAPI PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version}: 'Update the status of a vocabulary version.'; OpenAPI POST .../versions 201: 'The previous active version is deprecated.'; SIMPL-18191/AC1: 'the system sets all previous versions of that vocabulary to DEPRECATED'; SIMPL-18172/AC2: 'all previous versions are automatically marked as DEPRECATED'.
findings.question: Is manual change of a version status in scope, may more than one version be ACTIVE, and does a new version deprecate all previous versions or only the active one?
options: Out of scope: only automatic status changes; one ACTIVE version at most
In scope: manual version status change allowed; a new version deprecates all older versions

findings.finding: The date filters do not say what a match is: the same day, the exact instant, or a from-date.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18164/AC1: 'supported filter and sort options on `name`, `status`, `creationDate` and `lastUpdated`'; OpenAPI CreationDateQuery: 'Filter by ISO 8601 creation date or date-time', pattern '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(T.*)?$'.
findings.question: For creationDate and lastUpdated, does a date match the whole day, does a date-time match exactly, or is it a lower bound?
options: Date matches the whole day (UTC); date-time matches exactly
Value is a lower bound (on or after)

findings.finding: The criterion rejects an unsupported filter field, but the OpenAPI does not say that unknown query parameters are refused; many frameworks ignore them.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18164/AC4: 'When I request vocabularies using an unsupported filter or sort field ... Then the API rejects the request with a validation error'; OpenAPI GET /vocabularies lists only name, status, creationDate, lastUpdated, sort, page, pageSize.
findings.question: Must an unknown query parameter (for example ?owner=x) return 400, or is only an unsupported sort value or invalid filter value rejected?
options: Unknown query parameters return 400
Unknown parameters are ignored; only invalid values of known parameters return 400

findings.finding: Pagination limits are not named: there is no maximum page size and no rule for a page past the last one.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18162/AC2: 'I ask with wrong query parameter for pagination Then Simpl-Open answers with error message 400'; OpenAPI PageSizeQuery: 'default: 20, minimum: 1' (no maximum); PageQuery 'minimum: 1'.
findings.question: What is the maximum pageSize, and what does a request for a page beyond totalPages return (200 with empty items, or 400)?
options: Maximum 100; page beyond the end returns 200 with empty items
No maximum; page beyond the end returns 400

findings.finding: The list row shows 'date created', 'last updated' and 'creator', but the API list returns the metadata of the latest version, so these could be values of the vocabulary or of its latest version.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18161/AC1: 'current version, vocabulary status (`Active`, `Deprecated`), date created, last updated, and creator'; OpenAPI GET /vocabularies: 'Get the latest version metadata for vocabularies.'
findings.question: Do 'date created' and 'creator' in the list mean when and by whom the vocabulary was first created, or the latest version?
options: Vocabulary: first version's creation date and creator
Latest version's creation date and creator

findings.finding: The UI list story does not cover an empty list or more vocabularies than one page, while the API is paginated with a default of 20.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18161/AC1: 'I see a list of all vocabularies'; OpenAPI GET /vocabularies: page, pageSize default 20, 'Empty result sets return an empty `items` array'.
findings.question: Does the UI page through the list (and with which page size), and what does it show when there are no vocabularies?
options: UI pages with 20 rows and shows an empty-state message
UI loads all pages at once

findings.finding: The criterion does not say which columns are sortable or how the direction is chosen. The list shows eight columns, the API sorts on four.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18163/AC2: 'I click on a sortable column header ... ordered according to that column in ascending or descending order'; SIMPL-18161/AC1 columns include description, current version, creator; OpenAPI VocabularyListSortQuery: name, status, creationDate, lastUpdated.
findings.question: Which columns are sortable, what is the default order, and does a second click reverse the direction?

findings.finding: 'Full details' of a downloaded version can mean the Turtle content only or the content plus metadata, and 'review its full details' has no observable outcome.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18165/AC1: 'I can download the newest version of that vocabulary And I can review its full details'; SIMPL-18452/AC2: 'the system provides a file containing the full details of the selected version'; OpenAPI GET /content/{vocabularyName} and /content/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version}: 'Turtle content'.
findings.question: Is the download the Turtle file as returned by /content, and where does the user 'review full details' (a details screen, or the file)?
options: Download is the Turtle file only; details are on the details page
Download includes metadata in the file

findings.finding: 'I can access that selected version' does not say what is shown, so there is no pass condition.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18452/AC1: 'When I open a vocabulary and select a specific version for review Then I can access that selected version'.
findings.question: What does the user see after selecting a version (which fields, which actions)?

findings.finding: The criterion asks for structure and metadata in one answer, while the API operation for a version returns metadata only and serves the content through a separate download.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18166/AC1: 'the API returns the complete structure and metadata in a machine-readable format'; OpenAPI GET /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version}: 'Get metadata for a specific vocabulary version.' (VocabularyMetadata with contentHref); GET /content/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version}: 'text/turtle'.
findings.question: Is the criterion met by the metadata response with a contentHref link to the Turtle content, or must one response carry both?
options: Metadata JSON with contentHref; content via /content (as in the OpenAPI)
One response with metadata and content

findings.finding: 'Chronological' does not give the direction, and opening 'the history' leads to 'the vocabulary details page', which other stories call the history page.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18167/AC1: 'Then I am redirected to the vocabulary details page And I see a chronological list of all versions'; SIMPL-18559/AC1: 'the vocabulary history page'.
findings.question: Is the version list newest first or oldest first, and are the details page and the history page the same screen?
options: Newest first; one screen
Oldest first; one screen

findings.finding: The history story has no criterion for a load failure or a vocabulary that is not found, while the list story has one for errors.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18167 has one criterion (positive path only); SIMPL-18161/AC2: 'I am informed that the vocabulary list could not be loaded'; OpenAPI GET /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions: 404, 500.
findings.question: What does the history page show when loading fails or the vocabulary is not found?

findings.finding: The criterion asks for a list of all versions with 'metadata needed for comparison', while the API returns a paginated list with a fixed field set.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18168/AC1: 'the API returns a structured list of all versions with metadata needed for comparison'; OpenAPI GET /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions: page, pageSize (default 20), items VocabularyMetadata.
findings.question: Is a paginated answer acceptable for 'all versions', and which fields count as 'metadata needed for comparison'?
options: Paginated, VocabularyMetadata fields as in the OpenAPI
All versions in one response

findings.finding: The criterion assumes the user can search and filter vocabulary versions, but no UI story and no API operation offers search or filter on versions.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18176/AC2: 'When I search, filter, or browse vocabulary versions'; OpenAPI GET /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions parameters: sort, page, pageSize only.
findings.question: Is browsing the history of one vocabulary enough, or is a search or filter over versions required?
options: Browse only (history page)
Add a version filter (for example by status)

findings.finding: The criterion shows the creator of a version, but the API version metadata has no creator field.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18176/AC3: 'all associated metadata (e.g., version identifier, creation date, creator, change summary)'; OpenAPI VocabularyMetadata properties: href, contentHref, latestVersionHref, name, version, description, changelog, status, creationDate, lastUpdateDate (no createdBy).
findings.question: Should version metadata include createdBy, or is the creator not shown for versions?
options: Add createdBy to VocabularyMetadata
Drop creator from the version view

findings.finding: The criterion does not say where the warning appears or what it looks like, and the list already shows the status, so a tester cannot tell what passes.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18178/AC1: 'When I see a deprecated vocabulary Then the system shows a clear warning message indicating deprecation'; SIMPL-18161/AC1 already shows 'vocabulary status (`Active`, `Deprecated`)'.
findings.question: On which screens is the warning shown (list row, details page, download), in which form (icon, banner, tooltip), and with what text?

findings.finding: The UI has no control to select a referenced vocabulary version; references are inside the uploaded file. It is unclear when the warning appears.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18184/AC4: 'When I select or reference a vocabulary version with status _DEPRECATED_ Then Simpl-Open displays a clear warning'; SIMPL-18172/AC2 form: metadata, change summary, file; OpenAPI warning location: 'prefix 'legacy' -> 'https://authority.example/vocabulary-manager/content/LegacyVocabulary/versions/1#''.
findings.question: Is the warning shown after the file is uploaded or submitted (from the API warnings), or does the form need a picker for referenced vocabularies?
options: Show the API warnings after submission
Add a referenced-vocabulary picker to the form

findings.finding: The status check covers only new versions, while the process asks for it on new vocabularies too, and the criteria do not say how a reference to an internal vocabulary version is recognised in the file.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18184 I want: 'check the status of vocabulary versions I reuse when creating a new version'; BP 2B.4.3: 'verifies the status of the vocabularies used to create a new vocabulary or a new version of a vocabulary'; SIMPL-18184 notes: 'this is only for INTERNAL vocabularies'; OpenAPI warning location uses the contentHref URL as namespace.
findings.question: Does the deprecated-reference check also run on POST /vocabularies, and is a reference internal when its namespace equals a vocabulary contentHref (latest or versioned)?

findings.finding: The pass condition 'the API response or processing state indicates that syntax validation has passed' has no field in the API, and 'or' leaves two places to look.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18181/AC1: 'the API response or processing state indicates that syntax validation has passed'; OpenAPI 201 VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse has no validation status field; SIMPL-18194/AC2: 'confirms successful validation as part of the creation ... response without separate error details'.
findings.question: Is a 201 response the indicator that syntax validation passed, or is a field needed?
options: 201 Created is the indicator
Add a validation status field to the response

findings.finding: 'not created as an ACTIVE vocabulary' suggests the vocabulary could still be stored in another state after a syntax error.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18181/AC2: 'the vocabulary is not created as an ACTIVE vocabulary And no new ACTIVE version is created'; SIMPL-18183/AC2: 'the vocabulary or vocabulary version is not created'; OpenAPI 400 VocabularyValidationBadRequestResponse.
findings.question: After a syntax error, is nothing stored at all, or is a non-active record kept?
options: Nothing is stored
A non-active (draft or rejected) record is stored

findings.finding: The field format rules and the error messages are not named in the story, so 'field formats are correct' and 'appropriate error messages' have no oracle. The API has the name rule.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18169/AC2: 'Field formats are correct', 'if validation fails, I am informed with appropriate error messages in the UI'; OpenAPI CreateVocabularyPayload.name: 'minLength: 3, maxLength: 64, pattern: ^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$'.
findings.question: Which format rules apply per field (name as in the OpenAPI? description length?), is uniqueness case-sensitive, and where is each error shown (per field or as one message)?

findings.finding: The API create story has no criterion for a duplicate name, a file that is too large, or a wrong content type, which the OpenAPI answers with 409, 413 and 415. The same gaps apply to new versions in SIMPL-18173.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18170/AC3 covers only 'invalid or incomplete data'; OpenAPI POST /vocabularies responses '409', '413', '415'; SIMPL-18169/AC2: 'The vocabulary name is unique'.
findings.question: Confirm that a duplicate name returns 409, an oversized file 413 and a wrong content type 415, as in the OpenAPI.

findings.finding: 'Unsupported format' can mean a wrong request content type (415) or a file that is not Turtle (400).
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18173/AC6: 'Given I submit the request in an unsupported format When the system cannot process the request Then the request is rejected'; OpenAPI POST .../versions: 415 'Request content type is not supported', 400 'invalid vocabulary file content'.
findings.question: Which case does this criterion test, and which status code is expected?
options: Wrong request content type, 415
Non-Turtle file, 400

findings.finding: Neither status story says what happens when the requested status equals the current one; the OpenAPI answers 409 for that case.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18175/AC1: 'updates the vocabulary status to the requested value'; SIMPL-18174/AC1: 'I choose `ACTIVE` or `DEPRECATED`'; OpenAPI ConflictResponse example: 'Vocabulary is already in status ACTIVE'.
findings.question: Does a request for the current status return 409 (API) and does the UI offer only the other status?
options: 409 Conflict; UI offers only the other status
200 with no change (idempotent)

findings.finding: 'hidden or disabled' gives two behaviours, and an error on an attempt is only possible if the action is visible.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18195/AC2: 'restricted actions are hidden or disabled And attempts to perform restricted actions display an authorization error message'.
findings.question: Are restricted actions hidden or shown disabled, and when does the authorization error message appear (for example on a direct URL)?
options: Hidden; error only on direct navigation
Disabled; error on click

findings.finding: The UI report story covers errors only. The API can return non-blocking warnings on success, and the story does not say whether or how the UI shows them.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18193/AC2: 'I cannot complete the flow until the blocking validation errors are resolved'; OpenAPI VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse.validationWarnings: 'Non-blocking validation warnings returned when vocabulary creation succeeds despite warnings.'
findings.question: Does the UI show validation warnings after a successful creation, and where?

findings.finding: The story has no Given/When/Then criteria and an open question with the customer. It is unclear whether this component must ship the CPSV vocabulary as seed data.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-393 AC: 'The onthology is visible while executing endpoint to fetch all onthologies', 'We are able to fetch details of stored onthology'; note: 'to de defined with customer, whether it is enough, that the mentioned schemas are already provided as initial setup in the catalogues ... or whether a generic solution ... is requested'.
findings.question: Must Vocabulary Manager be deployed with the Core Public Services vocabulary pre-loaded, and is GET /vocabularies listing it the acceptance test?
options: Pre-load CPSV as seed data
No seed data; the generic upload covers it

findings.finding: The story has no criteria, is still in grooming, and asks for things the other stories and the API do not have: removing a vocabulary and a UI that wraps the catalogue's vocabulary calls.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-395: 'Ovi will add further Subtasks + AC'; 'the user can either remove the vocabulary from the catalogue or download the vocabulary/schema'; 'the UI should wrap the vocabulary calls of the catalogue'; BP02B.05: 'Deprecation does not mean deletion'; OpenAPI has no DELETE for internal vocabularies.
findings.question: Is SIMPL-395 replaced by the SIMPL-181xx stories, or does it still add a requirement (deletion, catalogue integration)?
options: Replaced; nothing to build from it
Still adds deletion or catalogue integration

findings.finding: The same actor appears under several names.
findings.evidence: 'Governance Authority' (most stories), 'Governance Authority user' (SIMPL-18169, 18172, 18189, 18191), 'governance authority agent' (SIMPL-393, 395), 'Governance Authority End User' (SIMPL-28680), 'user with the _Vocabulary Management_ role' (SIMPL-18181).
findings.question: Can all of these be read as one actor, the Governance Authority user?

findings.finding: Screen names vary: management page, management screen, details page, history page, history interface.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18161/AC1: 'Vocabulary Management screen'; SIMPL-18165/AC1: 'Vocabulary Management page'; SIMPL-18167/AC1: 'vocabulary details page'; SIMPL-18559/AC1: 'vocabulary history page'; SIMPL-18176/AC1: 'vocabulary management or history interface'.
findings.question: Which screens exist (list, details with history), and which name should the criteria use?

findings.finding: Field names differ between stories and the API.
findings.evidence: SIMPL-18164/AC1 filter '`lastUpdated`' vs SIMPL-18162/AC1 and OpenAPI field 'lastUpdateDate'; SIMPL-18172/AC2 'change summary', SIMPL-18167/AC1 'Change log', OpenAPI 'changelog'; SIMPL-18161/AC1 'creator', OpenAPI 'createdBy'.
findings.question: Confirm the pairs mean the same field.

findings.finding: The vocabulary has three names: 'vocabulary' in the stories and the process, InternalVocabulary in the CDM and VocabularyCategory in the API. 'Category' appears in no story, no process step and no CDM class. The schema also mixes two CDM classes: it is described as the latest version metadata, but it carries the vocabulary-level status. A builder cannot tell whether this object is the vocabulary or a view of its latest version.
findings.evidence: CDM:vocabulary-manager-be:InternalVocabulary ('Identified by a unique `name`; `latestVersion` identifies the most recently created version; `status` is the vocabulary-level lifecycle status'); OpenAPI GET /vocabularies summary 'Get the latest version metadata for vocabularies.' with items VocabularyCategory; GET /vocabularies/{vocabularyName} 'Get the latest metadata for a vocabulary.' returns VocabularyCategory; PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName} 'Update the status of an existing vocabulary.' returns VocabularyCategory; VocabularyCategory fields 'version', 'createdBy' have no CDM attribute of that name (CDM has latestVersion, no creator); SIMPL-18161/AC1 'a list of all vocabularies'; SIMPL-18175/AC1 'responds with the updated vocabulary metadata'.
findings.question: Is the object returned by GET /vocabularies, GET and PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName} the vocabulary itself (CDM InternalVocabulary), or a read view of its latest version, and which one name should the CDM and the API use for it?
options: It is the vocabulary: name the CDM class and the schema Vocabulary, and rename the field version to latestVersion (stories use 'vocabulary' most)
It is the vocabulary: keep the CDM name InternalVocabulary and rename the schema to InternalVocabulary
It is a read view of the latest version: add it to the CDM as a named read model (as Schema Manager does with SchemaMetadata) and name the schema after it, for example VocabularySummary

findings.finding: The vocabulary version has four names: 'vocabulary version' in the stories, InternalVocabularyVersion in the CDM, and VocabularyMetadata, VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse and (in part) VocabularySearchItem in the API. The API name VocabularyMetadata also clashes with the stories, where 'vocabulary metadata' means the vocabulary-level data (DDD-02).
findings.evidence: CDM:vocabulary-manager-be:InternalVocabularyVersion; OpenAPI GET and PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version} return VocabularyMetadata; GET /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions returns items VocabularyMetadata; POST /vocabularies and POST /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions return VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse (same fields plus validationWarnings, without latestVersionHref); POST /vocabularies/searches returns VocabularySearchItem; SIMPL-18166/AC1 'a specific vocabulary version'; SIMPL-18176/AC2 'vocabulary versions marked as DEPRECATED'; SIMPL-18452/AC1 'select a specific version'; SIMPL-18162 title 'Retrieve metadata of all vocabularies via API' (answered by VocabularyCategory, not VocabularyMetadata); SIMPL-18172/AC1 'pre-filled with the existing vocabulary metadata'.
findings.question: Which one name should the version carry in the CDM and the API, and is the creation response a separate concept or the same version object with warnings attached?
options: VocabularyVersion in CDM and API (stories say 'vocabulary version'); the 201 response is VocabularyVersion plus a validationWarnings list, named as a wrapper
Keep the CDM name InternalVocabularyVersion and use it for the API schema too

findings.finding: The CDM uses 'validation warning' for two concepts: blocking errors and non-blocking warnings. Its warning codes include syntaxError and semanticError, which the API treats as blocking errors (400, no vocabulary created). The API keeps them apart: VocabularyValidationIssue in the 400 report, VocabularyValidationWarning in the 201 response. The API warning code deprecatedVocabularyReference is not in the CDM value set. A code writer working from the CDM would return syntax errors as warnings on a created version.
findings.evidence: CDM VocabularyValidationWarning: 'A validation issue or non-fatal problem detected during Turtle syntax check, semantic validation, or OWL consistency reasoning'; CDM value set 'VocabularyValidationWarning.warningCode: syntaxError, semanticError, externalReferenceSkipped, semanticReasoningSkipped'; OpenAPI VocabularyValidationBadRequestResponse examples 'syntaxError', 'semanticError' (400, issues of VocabularyValidationIssue); OpenAPI VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse.validationWarnings 'Non-blocking validation warnings returned when vocabulary creation succeeds despite warnings', example codes 'externalReferenceSkipped' and 'deprecatedVocabularyReference'; SIMPL-18193/AC2 'blocking validation errors'; SIMPL-18183 note 'we issue warnings for external vocabularies that cannot be resolved'.
findings.question: Are blocking validation errors and non-blocking validation warnings two concepts, and what is the full code set of each?
options: Two CDM concepts: VocabularyValidationError (listed in the validation report, blocks creation) and VocabularyValidationWarning (returned with the created version), each with its own code set
One CDM concept VocabularyValidationIssue with a severity (error or warning) and one code set; API schemas named after it

findings.finding: The validation report is a business concept in the process and the stories, but the CDM has no class for it, and it has five names across the sources. The API carries it in an error wrapper, which is fine as a transport, but the concept behind it is missing from the CDM.
findings.evidence: BP02B.06 'Simpl-Open sends a report to the Governance Authority highlighting any validation issues detected'; 2B.4.4 'receives a notification about vocabulary validation errors'; SIMPL-18193 title 'Receive vocabulary validation report via UI'; SIMPL-18194/AC1 'a structured report listing all errors'; SIMPL-18182/AC3 'a structured report detailing semantic errors'; SIMPL-18181/AC2 'a structured error response'; SIMPL-18173/AC2 'rejected with validation feedback'; OpenAPI VocabularyValidationProblem (400); CDM 'Validation results are computed during version creation but not persisted as metadata'.
findings.question: Should the CDM name the validation report as a (transient) concept, and which name should the stories and the API use?
options: Add 'validation report' to the CDM as a transient value object listing validation errors; keep VocabularyValidationProblem as its transport and say so
Leave it out of the CDM as a pure transport; settle the story wording on 'validation report' only

findings.finding: The vocabulary reference drives the status check of the process and the deprecation warning, but the CDM has no concept for it. It is not stated how a reference inside the uploaded content identifies an internal vocabulary version. The API examples suggest the namespace of an internal version is its content URL, while the CDM gives a namespace only to external vocabularies.
findings.evidence: 2B.4.3 'verifies the status of the vocabularies used to create a new vocabulary'; SIMPL-18184/AC1 'I reference one or more existing vocabulary versions'; SIMPL-18184/AC3 'I reference a vocabulary version that does not exist'; OpenAPI warning location "prefix 'legacy' -> 'https://authority.example/vocabulary-manager/content/LegacyVocabulary/versions/1#'"; OpenAPI searchVocabularies 'for semantic reference resolution'; ExternalVocabularyContentRequest.namespaceUri 'Namespace URI as used in the vocabulary definition prefix'; CDM InternalVocabulary has no namespace attribute, ExternalVocabulary has namespaceUri; context CDM schema-manager-be: 'Schema Manager calls Vocabulary Manager to resolve vocabulary references and validate namespace URIs'.

options: Add VocabularyReference (namespace URI found in the content) to the CDM, resolving to an internal vocabulary version by its content URL or to an external vocabulary by namespace or alias URI
Give InternalVocabularyVersion a namespaceUri attribute and define the reference as a namespace URI match, in the CDM text

findings.finding: 'Latest version' can mean two things: the most recently created version (CDM, API), or the most recent ACTIVE version (stories). The stories also say 'current' and 'newest'. Once a version status can be changed by hand, the latest version may be DEPRECATED, and the two meanings give different results for the list, the download and the search.
findings.evidence: CDM InternalVocabulary: '`latestVersion` identifies the most recently created version'; OpenAPI VocabularySearchItem.latest 'True when the result came from latest vocabulary metadata'; GET /content/{vocabularyName} 'Download the latest vocabulary content'; VocabularyMetadata.latestVersionHref; SIMPL-18170/AC1 'version `1` as the latest version'; SIMPL-18161/AC1 'current version'; SIMPL-18165/AC1 'the newest version of that vocabulary'; SIMPL-18184/AC2 'recommends using the latest _ACTIVE_ version'; SIMPL-18559/AC1 'a more recent ACTIVE version', 'the latest ACTIVE version'; OpenAPI PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version}.
findings.question: Does 'latest version' mean the highest version number whatever its status, or the most recent ACTIVE version, and should 'current' and 'newest' be retired?
options: Latest version = highest version number, whatever its status; 'latest ACTIVE version' is a separate, explicit term
Latest version = most recent ACTIVE version; the CDM text and the API descriptions change to match

findings.finding: The states of the vocabulary and of the version are listed in the CDM, but the allowed transitions are not written down in one place, and the CDM text and the stories differ on what a new version deprecates. Each operation that changes a status cannot be checked against a transition table.
findings.evidence: CDM value sets 'InternalVocabulary.status: ACTIVE, DEPRECATED', 'InternalVocabularyVersion.status: ACTIVE, DEPRECATED'; CDM relationship note 'Creating an InternalVocabularyVersion makes it ACTIVE and deprecates the previous active version'; SIMPL-18191/AC1 'sets all previous versions of that vocabulary to DEPRECATED'; SIMPL-18172/AC2 and SIMPL-18173/AC1 'all previous versions'; SIMPL-18170/AC2 'can later be manually changed to `DEPRECATED` or back to `ACTIVE`'; BP02B.05 'Full Vocabulary Deprecation - all versions deprecated when obsolete'; OpenAPI ConflictResponse 'Vocabulary is already in status ACTIVE'; CDM open question SIMPL-18201 (reason and effective date for status changes).
findings.question: Can the spec owners add one transition table per entity (vocabulary, vocabulary version) next to the CDM, naming for each transition the operation and the criteria that cause it?
options: Add a state table to the CDM: vocabulary ACTIVE <-> DEPRECATED by PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}; version created ACTIVE by POST, ACTIVE -> DEPRECATED by a new version or by PATCH .../versions/{version}; same-status request gives 409
Drop the manual version transition and keep only the automatic one, then write the table

findings.finding: The identity of an external vocabulary is stated two ways. The CDM says it is identified by its canonical namespace URI (plus aliases); the API addresses it by name in every path and also looks up its content by namespace URI. For the internal vocabulary the identity is the name, but it is called vocabularyName in paths and name in bodies, queries and the search, while the external path parameter is called name.
findings.evidence: CDM ExternalVocabulary: 'Identified by a canonical namespace URI and zero or more alias URIs'; OpenAPI paths /external-vocabularies/{name}, /external-vocabularies/{name}/content, Location '/external-vocabularies/DublinCoreTerms'; POST /external-vocabularies/content 'Resolves the cached external vocabulary by the namespace URI'; ExternalVocabularyNotFoundResponse "External vocabulary with namespaceUri 'http://purl.org/dc/terms' was not found."; parameters VocabularyNamePath 'vocabularyName', ExternalVocabularyNamePath 'name', VocabularyNameQuery 'name'; CreateVocabularyPayload.name; VocabularySearchItemRequest.name.
findings.question: Is an external vocabulary identified by its name or by its namespace URI, and should the name parameter of both vocabulary kinds use one spelling?
options: Name is the identity for both kinds; the namespace URI and aliases are unique lookup keys; the CDM text says so
Namespace URI is the identity of an external vocabulary; the name is a label; paths keep the name as a convenience key, written down as such

findings.finding: The CDM of this component and the context CDM of Schema Manager exist and point to their APIs, but neither is approved for delivery. A glossary built on them can still change.

Keep the API names and record the story words as UI labels with a written mapping (DDD-05)

findings.finding: The creator is in the API and the stories but not in the CDM. The API example is a person's e-mail address, while the CDM relation names the Governance Authority, an organisation role, as the one who creates vocabularies.

findings.finding: 'Description' names two attributes: one of the vocabulary and one of each version. options: One description per version; the vocabulary shows the latest version's description (remove InternalVocabulary.description)
Separate descriptions; the version request sets only the version description

findings.finding: The vocabulary content has several names (rdfContent, vocabularyFile, content, file, full details), and the CDM class ExternalVocabulary has no content attribute although the API stores and serves its content.

options: Term 'vocabulary content'; CDM attribute content on both vocabulary version and external vocabulary; vocabularyFile stays as the form field name, written down
Keep rdfContent in the CDM and map it in the glossary

findings.finding: GovernanceAuthority is marked as an external actor with an attribute, and the Schema Manager CDM defines it the same way, but neither names the context that owns it. The roles that control access (GA_VOCABULARY_VIEWER, GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN) are not referenced in the CDM.

findings.finding: There is no context map in the input. The two CDMs reference each other in their traceability tables and agree on the direction (Schema Manager consumes Vocabulary Manager), but the register's concept ownership index is not part of the snapshot, and the Metadata Quality Profile vocabulary dependency named in SIMPL-28680 appears in neither CDM.

Accept the pairwise traceability tables as the context map for this component

findings.finding: Adding an external vocabulary is called registration in the process and the CDM, but creation, caching and copying in the API. No story covers registering, reading or deleting an external vocabulary, so the term has no criteria to settle it.

ExternalVocabulary : registers', 'ExternalVocabulary registration'; OpenAPI POST /external-vocabularies 'Create a cached external vocabulary for validation', tag 'Manage copied external vocabularies'; DELETE /external-vocabularies/{name} 'Hard deletes'; inventory-review.md: external vocabulary operations are covered only by the blanket criteria of SIMPL-18196.
findings.question: Is 'register an external vocabulary' the term for POST /external-vocabularies, and which story will hold the criteria for it?
options: 'register' (process and CDM); 'cached copy' stays as the definition, not as a second verb
'create' to match the API, and the CDM and process wording follow

findings.finding: The two search operations have no story and no decision, and their contract is open on the points a tester needs. Both responses extend CollectionPage (page, pageSize, total, totalPages), but neither request takes page or pageSize, and the request arrays have no maxItems. One builder returns every match in one response, another cuts at the default page size of 20 and drops the rest without a way to fetch them. The result order, the handling of duplicate references, and the outcome of an external search body that matches more than one oneOf branch (for example namespaceUri plus namespaceUris) are not stated either.
findings.evidence: OpenAPI POST /vocabularies/searches: request VocabularySearchRequest (items, minItems 1, no maxItems, no page parameters), response VocabularySearchResponse allOf CollectionPage, example 'page: 1, pageSize: 20, total: 2, totalPages: 1'; POST /external-vocabulary/searches: request ExternalVocabularySearchRequest (oneOf namespaceUri | aliasUri | anyOf namespaceUris, aliasUris; arrays without maxItems), response GetExternalVocabularyListResponse with page/pageSize; links.json: both operations are linked only by SIMPL-18196/AC1 to AC4 ('invoke any Vocabulary Management API endpoint'); decisions D16 (role only) and D22 (pagination limits, worded for GET) do not cover them.
findings.question: Are the search results paged, how many references may one request hold, in which order are results returned, and is a body that fits two oneOf branches rejected?
options: No paging: all matches in one response with page 1, totalPages 1 and pageSize equal to the number of items; at most 100 references per request (400 above); results in request order, duplicates removed; a body that fits two branches returns 400
Paging as on the GET lists: page and pageSize query parameters on the POST, default 20, maximum 100; results ordered by name then version; duplicates removed; two branches return 400

findings.finding: Step 30 decided several behaviours that the OpenAPI file does not yet show. A builder who generates server stubs, clients or contract tests from the file builds the old behaviour: no 401 or 403 responses, a strict PascalCase name filter, an unbounded pageSize, no creator on version objects, an optional validationWarnings with a free-text code, unbounded description and changelog, a version form field that the schema does not forbid, a nullable latestVersionHref, and silence on unknown query parameters.
findings.evidence: D17 (401 urn:problem-type:simpl:unauthorized, 403 urn:problem-type:simpl:forbidden) vs every operation: responses limited to 200/201/204, 400, 404, 406, 409, 413, 415, 500; D19 (name filter ^[A-Za-z0-9]+$, minLength 1, contains match) vs components/parameters/VocabularyNameQuery pattern '^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$', minLength 3; D22 (pageSize maximum 100) vs PageSizeQuery 'minimum: 1' only; D27 (createdBy on version objects) vs schemas VocabularyMetadata and VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse without createdBy; D10 (validationWarnings always present, closed code set externalReferenceSkipped, deprecatedVocabularyReference, semanticReasoningSkipped) vs VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse without required list and VocabularyValidationWarning.code 'type: string' without enum; D37 (description and changelog 1 to 1000 characters) vs CreateVocabularyPayload and CreateNewVocabularyVersionPayload without minLength or maxLength; D7 (version form field returns 400) vs CreateNewVocabularyVersionPayload without additionalProperties false; D5 (latestVersionHref always filled) vs VocabularyMetadata.latestVersionHref 'nullable: true'; D21 (unknown query parameter returns 400) not stated on any GET.

findings.finding: The security scheme does not fit the decided access model. It declares an OAuth2 authorization code flow with placeholder URLs and two scopes, read and write, while D16 grants access by two Keycloak realm roles and states that the scopes are not checked. A client generated from the file will ask for scopes that mean nothing, and a builder can reasonably enforce read and write scopes instead of the roles. SEC-07 asks for OpenID Connect through the Tier 1 Keycloak; the file names neither.
findings.evidence: components/securitySchemes/OAuth2Auth: type oauth2, flows.authorizationCode, authorizationUrl 'https://auth.example.com/oauth/authorize', tokenUrl 'https://auth.example.com/oauth/token', scopes 'read: Read access', 'write: Write access', description 'OAuth2 authentication provided by the gateway.'; top-level security '- OAuth2Auth: []'; D16 'GA_VOCABULARY_VIEWER', 'GA_VOCABULARY_ADMIN', 'The OAuth2 scopes read and write in the OpenAPI are not checked.'; D17 'The service validates the bearer token ... and the roles itself'; E1 realm 'simpl'.

findings.finding: Seven operations are reached by no acceptance criterion except the blanket access rules of SIMPL-18196. For six of them, the external vocabulary operations, no story exists at all; D30 fixes their behaviour, but there are no criteria for listing, reading, reading content by name or deleting an external vocabulary. The manual version status change is decided in D4 but also has no story. 21a counted these operations as covered because the inferred SIMPL-18196 links point at every secured operation.
findings.evidence: links.json: GET /external-vocabularies, POST /external-vocabularies, GET /external-vocabularies/{name}, GET /external-vocabularies/{name}/content, DELETE /external-vocabularies/{name} and PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version} have links only from SIMPL-18196/AC1 to AC4 (reason "'invoke any Vocabulary Management API endpoint' with the role"); SIMPL-18166 names the path of the PATCH but its links point at the GET only; D-020 'No story covers registering, reading or deleting an external vocabulary'; F-015; D4; D30.
findings.question: Which story holds the acceptance criteria for registering, listing, reading and deleting external vocabularies, and for the manual version status change?
options: Add one API story for external vocabulary registration (create, list, read, content, delete) and one for the version status change, with criteria taken from D30 and D4
Accept D30 and D4 as the test basis for this build and record the missing stories as a backlog item

findings.finding: The external vocabulary operations reuse error responses written for internal vocabularies. GET and DELETE /external-vocabularies/{name} answer 404 with VocabularyNotFoundResponse, whose example says 'Vocabulary with name' and points the issue at a path parameter 'vocabularyName' that these paths do not have, while ExternalVocabularyNotFoundResponse exists. POST /external-vocabularies answers 400 with VocabularyValidationBadRequestResponse, whose examples include a semantic error, while D30 says registration checks syntax only. Two builders will word these bodies differently, and tests that check the issue name will fail on one of them.
findings.evidence: OpenAPI GET and DELETE /external-vocabularies/{name} '404: $ref VocabularyNotFoundResponse'; VocabularyNotFoundResponse example issues 'in: path, name: vocabularyName'; ExternalVocabularyNotFoundResponse used only by POST /external-vocabularies/content and GET /external-vocabularies/{name}/content; POST /external-vocabularies '400: $ref VocabularyValidationBadRequestResponse' with example semanticError; D30 'Registration checks Turtle syntax only (400 on error), no semantic validation'.

findings.finding: GET /external-vocabularies is paged but has no sort parameter and no stated default order, so the content of page 2 differs between builders. D23 fixes the order only for the internal vocabulary lists.
findings.evidence: OpenAPI GET /external-vocabularies parameters PageQuery and PageSizeQuery only; D23 'GET /vocabularies ... default is name ascending', 'GET .../versions default order is version number descending'.
findings.question: What is the default order of GET /external-vocabularies?
options: name ascending, as GET /vocabularies
creationDate descending

findings.finding: Path naming is not consistent. Literal segments use kebab-case instead of lowerCamelCase. The external search path uses a singular 'external-vocabulary' next to the plural 'external-vocabularies', which is easy to get wrong. Internal content lives under a separate root /content/{vocabularyName}, while external content lives under the resource, /external-vocabularies/{name}/content. Controller segments share a level with identifiers: GET /vocabularies/searches and GET /external-vocabularies/content fall into the {vocabularyName} and {name} templates and get 400 from the name pattern, or 405, depending on the router.
findings.evidence: Paths /external-vocabularies, /external-vocabularies/{name}, /external-vocabularies/{name}/content, /external-vocabularies/content, /external-vocabulary/searches, /vocabularies/searches, /content/{vocabularyName}, /content/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version}; API-06, API-10, API-28; A-002.

findings.finding: Identifier naming does not follow the guidelines and is not shared. The path parameters are vocabularyName and name, the resource property is name (API-50 asks for 'id' or 'code'), and there is no identifier schema type (API-54). The name pattern is written out five times, and D19 now relaxes one of the five copies, so a change can easily miss one. Since D30 makes the name the identity, a single VocabularyName schema referenced everywhere would keep the rule in one place.
findings.evidence: components/parameters VocabularyNamePath (vocabularyName), ExternalVocabularyNamePath (name), VocabularyNameQuery (name); pattern '^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$' repeated in VocabularyNamePath, ExternalVocabularyNamePath, VocabularyNameQuery, CreateVocabularyPayload.name, CreateExternalVocabularyPayload.name, VocabularySearchItemRequest.name; A-005; D-008; D30; D19.

findings.finding: Six bodies have no example. Four are the multipart upload requests, where an example form would show the field names and the Turtle file part. GET /external-vocabularies/{name} has no 200 example, and the two PATCH requests have none.
findings.evidence: A-003: POST /vocabularies, POST /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions, POST /external-vocabularies (multipart/form-data); PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}, PATCH /vocabularies/{vocabularyName}/versions/{version} (application/json); GET /external-vocabularies/{name} 200.

findings.finding: info.description states a business purpose but covers only part of the API. It speaks of internal vocabularies, while the API also registers external vocabularies and offers reference search for other components.
findings.evidence: info.description 'This API allows the Governance Authority to manage internal vocabularies.'; tags 'External vocabulary management'; POST /vocabularies/searches 'for semantic reference resolution'.

findings.finding: POST /external-vocabularies/content is a read done with POST, and the API itself calls it legacy next to GET /external-vocabularies/{name}/content. No story covers it. If a consumer still resolves content by namespace URI it is plumbing and can stay; otherwise it is a candidate to retire.
findings.evidence: POST /external-vocabularies description 'the legacy `/external-vocabularies/content` endpoint remains available for namespace-based downloads'; POST /external-vocabularies/content 'Resolves the cached external vocabulary by the namespace URI'; links.json: only SIMPL-18196 links; D16 lists it as a read-only POST for the viewer role.
findings.question: Is the namespace-based content download still needed by a consumer in this build, or can it be retired?
options: Keep it as plumbing for namespace resolution and document why it is a POST
Retire it; consumers use POST /external-vocabulary/searches then GET /external-vocabularies/{name}/content

findings.finding: No response schema declares required properties, so every field is optional on the wire. A builder may leave out href, status or version, and a contract test cannot fail on a missing field. Only HealthResponse and the request schemas have required lists.
findings.evidence: Schemas VocabularyCategory, VocabularyMetadata, VocabularyVersionMetadataResponse, VocabularySearchItem, ExternalVocabulary, CollectionPage, Problem: no 'required'; HealthResponse 'required: status'.
